How to use X forwarding with SSH. A very useful trick
Vnc is almost always a better alternative to x forwarding.

X forwarding worked great in the past when applications were relatively simple and didn't have a lot of X calls. They were basically written with "non-local X" in mind.

These days not so much. Applications have decorations and over the top X calls, and are written / optimized with "running X on the same computer" in mind.

Because of that - even on LAN, using X forwarding to, e.g., run a web browser or even a graphical IDE, will barely work if at all.

I only skimmed the article, so it might be mentioned, but it's something to keep in mind nevertheless: whether you're using X-forwarding or VNC, a good best-practice is to only allow connections from localhost, and use SSH to proxy traffic accordingly.
